paragraphs.source_en:
‘S. transcribes his poem’ would at this point in the journal most probably refer to L&C, which
although finished on 23 September was still being transcribed for the printer in October (see
headnote to L&C). Nevertheless, in the absence of more conclusive evidence, the likeliest
assumption is that S. did himself produce a second version of Mont Blanc in the autumn of
1817, sometimes forgetting choices and substitutions he had made when copying from the draft
in the previous summer, and perhaps at times unable to read his own tangled draft. Two distinct
forms of the poem therefore exist, and are both presented here; the B text (1817) is collated with
Nbk 1 as this makes clear the extent to which it diverges from the draft relative to the A text
(SDMS), which is much closer to Nbk 1. Chernaik 288–93 offers a transcription of the draft.
